summary: Oxygen nuclear modification, generative TPC background simulation, and neural-network parton-density fits. The latest available arXiv announcement is dated 26 November; selected papers were submitted 25 November and fall outside the strict 24-hour window.
strongest_paper_summary: ALICE oxygen double ratio and production-integrated TPC fast simulation

papers.title: Nuclear Modification of π⁰ Production in pO and OO Collisions with ALICE
papers.abstract: Neutral-pion production in pO and OO collisions is measured with ALICE and compared with cold- and hot-matter calculations.
papers.summary: The OO-to-pO double ratio is suppressed by 4.9 standard deviations relative to an nNNPDF3.0 no-energy-loss baseline. The proceedings recaps an earlier ALICE measurement rather than presenting an independent new result.
papers.assessment: Strong experimental relevance; cold-matter cancellation depends on the baseline and different collision kinematics. The models shown do not resolve the energy-loss mechanism.

papers.title: Accelerating ALICE background simulations: A WGAN Approach to slow-neutron induced TPC loopers
papers.abstract: A Wasserstein generative adversarial network generates electron and positron backgrounds from slow-neutron interactions in the ALICE TPC, replacing expensive transport.
papers.summary: The model is integrated into ALICE simulation and the paper reports roughly tenfold acceleration of the relevant transport component, with comparisons to GEANT4.
papers.assessment: A practical, directly relevant application with production integration; the looper rate is separately normalized and momentum tails require attention. The timing gain is not an end-to-end speedup.

papers.title: Recent Developments in Colibri: A Neural-Network PDF Model and Improved Bayesian Sampling
papers.abstract: Colibri adds an open implementation of the n3fit neural-network PDF model and a BlackJAX nested sampler for comparing inference methods.
papers.summary: On 3,089 DIS pseudodata points, n3fit closure tests agree with NNPDF; the sampler comparison uses a 13-parameter polynomial model and yields consistent fit quality.
papers.assessment: A useful, quantitatively checked framework for controlled PDF methodology comparisons. The sampler benchmark is not an end-to-end Bayesian fit of the neural network, and direct nuclear-PDF application remains prospective.
